reading.body:
Tina Smith's recorded AI-related activity is almost entirely one bill, S. 2296, and she voted against it at every stage.

Ten of the fourteen events are votes on S. 2296, all cast on September 2, September 4, September 10, and October 9 of 2025. She voted Nay on cloture, on the motion to proceed, on the motion to table, and on final passage. The amendment votes are mixed, with five Yea and four Nay, but the procedural and passage votes are uniformly against. The two cosponsorships, S. 3682 and S. 2997, are the only affirmative items, and both are dated after the S. 2296 votes.

For AI specifically, the pattern matters because procedural votes decide whether a bill reaches the floor at all. A member who votes against cloture and against proceeding can stop a bill without ever recording a position on its substance. The amendment record shows she was willing to shape the bill, and the passage record shows she did not want it to advance in that form.

The data does not say what S. 2296 contained, what the amendments would have changed, or why any vote was cast. It also does not cover committee work, co-sponsorships that never received a status date, or anything outside this site's AI event set. The summary mentions money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, but no contribution events appear in the fourteen points, so the record here is legislative only.
